title: AXIOMA on Android: making an AI-assisted science deckbuilder readable on a phone
author: Typical-Instance-376
selftext:
I'm Samuel, the developer behind AXIOMA. I shared its Steam direction here before; this update is about the Android edition and a different challenge: making science cards worth reading on a small screen. This is my own commercial game.



The idea is to learn through play rather than stop the run for a lecture: scientific cards, formulas, scoring combinations and scientist wildcards become part of the strategy. I want that satisfying 'one more run' feeling, without claiming that playing guarantees better grades.



AI assistance is part of the development, including fixed illustrations, scientist portraits and supporting text/localization. The game is not generating new AI content live during a run. For this kind of project, a polished picture isn't enough: the formulas, card effects and relationships still need to make sense and remain readable.



The mobile design question interests me most: how much scientific detail can a card carry before the player stops reading it? The gameplay demo puts the cards, scoring and wildcards in focus, so you can judge that balance rather than just look at promotional art.



Gameplay: [https://www.instagram.com/quanta\_aulas/reel/DeHlS4lPuID/](https://www.instagram.com/quanta_aulas/reel/DeHlS4lPuID/)

Android: [https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.quantaaulas.axioma](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.quantaaulas.axioma)



For other AI-assisted game developers: how do you review factual assets and preserve legibility on mobile? Do you simplify the card itself, move explanations elsewhere, or let players inspect the full detail on demand?
